Example: There is a spell that says “Do this twice: Deal 3 to a unit.” Immortal
Phoenix is a unit that says “When you kill a unit with a spell, you may pay [1][C] to
play me from your trash.” A player plays the spell while Immortal Phoenix is in their
trash. The “do this” phrasing means that it has a reflexive triggered ability, which
places two triggered abilities on the chain. As each of those triggered abilities
resolve, it deals damage to the unit chosen for that ability. If one of these abilities
deals lethal damage to a unit, both the spell and its ability are considered sources
of the damage, and so both the spell and its ability receive attribution for killing the
unit. This means that the spell’s controller killed a unit with a spell, so Immortal
Phoenix’s ability will trigger.
429.6. This action is formatted as "Kill [one or more permanents]."
e.g., "Kill an enemy unit."
e.g., "Kill this, [2]: Draw 1."
e.g., "Kill all gear."

title: 430. Add
text:
430. Add
430.1. Adding is the action of putting resources into a player's Rune Pool.
430.2. Triggered and activated abilities that Add resources finalize immediately when they are played, even
when handling tasks or during the resolution of spells and abilities, and resolve as soon as they are
finalized.
430.2.a. Priority and Focus will not pass from Add abilities being finalized or resolving. Any ongoing
Task or step in the FEPR process is paused while they are being finalized and while they are
resolving.
430.2.b. Spells that Add resources will be finalized and will resolve at the normal timing for spells.
430.3. Activated abilities that Add resources and have the Reaction tag can be activated at any time that
spells or abilities require resources be paid.
Example: A player can add Energy and Power through any means before initiating the
process of playing a spell. After initiating that process, in the Pay Costs step, they may
activate Add Reactions to add Energy or Power to pay costs.
Example: A player moves two units to a battlefield where their opponent controls a
Mageseeker Investigator. Although they have no window of priority, they may activate Add
Reactions to pay for the applied cost from Mageseeker Investigator, and those abilities
finalize and resolve immediately.
430.4. Adding is a Limited Action.
430.4.a. Players may only Add resources when Game Effects direct them to do so.
430.5. This action is formatted as "Add [one or more resources]."
e.g., "Add [2]." means "Add 2 Energy."
e.g., "[E]: Add [Y]." means "Add 1 Power of the Order domain."
e.g., "Add [1][G]." means "Add 1 Energy and 1 Power of the Calm domain."

title: 431. Channel
text:
431. Channel
431.1. Channeling is the action of taking one or more Runes from the top of a player's Rune Deck and
putting them on the board.
431.2. The Game Effect that instructs a player to channel 1 or more runes may specify the conditions or
circumstances under which those runes enter the board.
Example: A spell reads "Channel 1 rune exhausted." As that spell resolves, its controller puts
the top rune of their rune deck onto the board and that rune enters the board exhausted
rather than ready.
431.2.a. By default, runes are channeled readied.
431.3. If there aren’t sufficient runes in the Rune Deck, channel as many as possible.
431.4. Channeling is a Limited Action.
431.4.a. A player Channels two Runes during the Channel Phase on their turn.
431.4.b. Players may also Channel runes when Game Effects direct them to do so.
431.5. This action is formatted as "Channel X rune(s)," optionally followed by conditions or stipulations.
e.g., "Channel 1 rune."
e.g., "When you play me, channel 1 rune exhausted."
e.g., "Channel 2 runes exhausted. If you couldn't channel 2 runes this way, draw 1."

title: 432. Burn Out
text:
432. Burn Out
432.1. Burning Out is an action a player must perform if they attempt to move one or more cards from
their Main Deck to any other zone in excess of the number of cards remaining in their Main Deck:
432.1.a. If a player must Draw cards in excess to the number of cards in their Main Deck, they will
Draw as many as possible, perform this action, then Draw the remaining amount
instructed.
432.1.b. If a player must put one or more cards from their Main Deck in any other zone, such as the
Trash, in excess of the number of cards in their deck they will do so as much as possible,
perform this action, and then complete the remaining number required by the instruction.
432.1.c. If an instruction directs a player to look at or reveal cards in excess to the number of cards in
a player’s Main Deck, that player looks at or Reveals as many as possible, but does not Burn
Out, then proceeds with the rest of the instruction.
432.1.c.1. If there are insufficient cards among the looked at or revealed cards to perform
subsequent actions to the revealed or looked at cards, any further instructions are
negated. This does not cause a Burn Out, even if those instructions would cause
those cards to change zones.
Reminder: Cards are considered in the zone of origin while being looked
at or revealed, in this case the Main Deck.
432.2. To Burn Out, a player does the following in sequence:
432.2.a. Performs as much of the prescribed action as possible.
432.2.b. Recycles their trash into their Main Deck.
Reminder: When multiple cards are Recycled to the Main Deck at the same time,
those cards must be randomized
432.2.c. Chooses an opponent to gain 1 point.
432.2.d. Completes the remainder of the action that caused them to burn out.
Example: A player attempts to draw 1 during their Draw Phase while their Main
Deck is empty. That player instead recycles their trash into their Main Deck,
randomizing it as normal, then chooses an opponent to gain 1 point, and then
draws 1.
432.3. A player's Main Deck may remain empty as they Burn Out, usually because their trash is also empty.
When they attempt to perform the original action again, it will cause another Burn Out.
432.3.a. Unless some effect intervenes, this will result in them burning out repeatedly, giving 1 point
to an opponent each time, until an opponent passes the Victory Score and wins the game.

title: 432. Burn Out
text:
432. Burn Out (continued)
432.3.b. Points gained after the first Burn Out being processed in sequence cannot be replaced or
prevented by any means.
432.3.c. Points gained after the first Burn Out being processed in sequence that cause a player to
reach or surpass the Victory Score for their game mode will cause that player to win the
game if they also have more points than every opponent.
Example: If a player has no cards in their deck or their trash and they go to draw 1,
they will begin to burn out repeatedly. After the first burn out is processed, any
subsequent burnout that brings a player to a number of points greater than the
Victory Score and more than any opponent will cause them to win the game.
432.3.c.1. The player wins immediately, without needing to wait for a cleanup to occur.
432.4. Burning Out is a Limited Action.
432.4.a. Players may only burn out when Game Effects direct them to do so.
432.5. Burning Out is a Replacement Effect.
See rule 367. Replacement Effects for more information.

title: 433. Double
text:
433. Double
433.1. Doubling is the act of increasing a numeric attribute by an amount equal to that attribute’s current
value.
433.1.a. This creates an effect that modulates that attribute by that specific amount for the duration
specified by the Game Effect that instructed the player to perform this action.
Example: A unit with 3 base Might and Shield 2 is in combat as a Defender. Since
Shield applies, its current Might is 5. A player chooses it as the target for Last Stand,
a spell that reads in part “Double a friendly unit's Might this turn.” Its current Might
is 5, so it gets +5 Might this turn, for a current Might of 10. After combat, Shield no
longer applies, but the +5 Might from Last Stand does, so the unit’s Might is 8.
433.1.b. Some Game Effects may also cause Damage to be Doubled; in this case, those effects are
the equivalent to a replacement effect that reads “If I would take damage from a source, I
take double that damage from that source instead.” or “If [I/this] would deal damage, [I/this]
deal double that damage instead.” The source of the Damage in these cases remains the
same after Doubling.
433.2. Doubling is a Limited Action.
433.2.a. Players may only Double when Game Effects direct them to do so.

title: 434. Swap
text:
434. Swap
434.1. Swapping is the act of increasing one numeric value and decreasing another numeric value on
some number of Game Objects such that their values are reversed.
434.1.a. Swapping creates two different effects that apply to each attribute. One that Increases one
value and one that Decreases the other. These effects last for the duration specified by the
effect that instructed the Swap.
434.1.b. To accomplish this, determine the difference between these values and then apply an
Increase for that amount to the lower value of the two attributes, and a Decrease of that
amount to the higher value of the two attributes.
434.1.c. If both attributes are the same numeric value, Swapping has no effect.
434.1.d. If the attributes being swapped are Units’ Mights, this effect is the equivalent to giving
those units a Might increasing effect and a Might decreasing effect respectively.
434.2. Swapping is a Limited Action.
434.2.a. Players may only swap when Game Effects direct them to do so.

title: 435. Attach
text:
435. Attach
435.1. Attaching is the act of linking two cards on the board together to combine their effects in some way.
This causes one or more cards to become Attached and at least one card to become a Top-Most
Card.
See rule 716. Attachment for more information.
435.1.a. Attaching affects two cards at once.
435.1.a.1. One card will be designated as the one being Attached, and thus become
Attached. The other will become the Top-Most Card.
435.1.b. This is represented by physically laying the Top-Most card on top of the other or others
such that all Effect Texts and Might Bonuses are showing, but nothing else from the card
or cards Attached.
435.1.b.1. In the situation where there is more than one card attached to the Top-Most card,
they should be stacked in such a way that all Effect Text boxes and Might
Bonuses are readable. The order of the Attached cards has no bearing on the
application of effects.
435.1.c. The Top-Most card has all Effect Text of all cards Attached to it appended to its Rules
Text.
435.1.d. The Top-Most Card has its Might modulated by the Might Bonus of all cards Attached to it.
435.1.e. Attaching one or more cards will cause those cards’ printed Rules Text to become Inactive
for as long as they remain Attached.
See rule 716. Attachment for more information.
435.1.f. Attaching a card to a new Top-Most Card will cause it to Detach from the card to which it
is currently Attached.
435.1.g. Attaching a card to its current Top-Most Card will not have any effect.
435.1.h. Units cannot be Attached to other cards.
See rule 140. Units for more information.
435.1.h.1. If a Unit would be Attached, nothing happens.
435.1.h.2. If a non-Unit Game Object that is attached becomes a Unit through any means, it
detaches as it becomes a Unit.
435.1.i. If a Game Effect instructs a player to Attach a card to its current Top-Most Card, nothing
additional happens.
435.2. Attaching is a Limited Action.
435.2.a. Players may only Attach cards when directed to by Game Effects.
435.3. Attaching cards does not inherently choose or specify a target. However, Game Effects that Attach
cards may do so.
435.4. When a card Attaches to a card, its location becomes the same as the new Top-Most Card.
435.4.a. This is not a Move.

title: 435. Attach
text:
435. Attach (continued)
435.5. Attaching a card to another card does not modify either card’s state except in making those cards
Attached and the Top-Most Card, and causing the Attached card to change locations.
Example: An exhausted equipment being attached to a unit does not ready the equipment.

title: 436. Detach
text:
436. Detach
436.1. Detaching is the act of unlinking two cards that are currently linked through the act of Attaching.
This causes one to cease being Attached, and potentially causes the other to cease being a Top-
Most card.
436.1.a. Detaching affects only cards that are currently Attached to another card.
436.1.a.1. Game effects that instruct a player to Detach a card that is currently not Attached
to anything will do nothing.
436.1.b. When one or more cards become Detached, they cease to be in the Attached state.
436.1.b.1. To represent this, these cards should no longer be placed under the card they
were previously placed under as Top-Most Card.
436.1.b.2. If the Top-Most Card no longer has any cards Attached to it after this, it is no
longer a Top-Most Card.
436.1.c. The card being Detached has its Effect Text become Inactive and its Rules Text cease
being Inactive.
436.1.d. The Top-Most Card ceases to have the Effect Text of the card being Detached appended
to its Rules Text.
436.1.e. The Top-Most Card ceases to have its Might modulated by the Might Bonus of the card
being Detached.
436.2. Detaching is a Limited Action.
436.2.a. Players may only Detach cards when directed to by Game Effects.
436.3. Detaching cards does not inherently choose, or specify a target. However, Game Effects that Detach
cards may.
436.4. When a card Detaches from a Top-Most Card, its location is the same as the Top-Most Card from
which it Detached.
436.4.a. If the Detached card was a Gear and this causes it to become present at a Battlefield, it will
be Recalled during the next Cleanup.
See rule 318. Cleanups for more information.
436.4.b. If the Attached card was Detached because the Top-Most Card changed zones from a
board zone to a non-board zone, then the location that the Attached Card will Detach to is
the last location the Top-Most Card was at before changing from a board zone to a non-
board zone.

title: 437. Predict
text:
437. Predict
437.1. Predicting a card is the act of looking at a single card from the top of the Main Deck and choosing
whether or not to Recycle it.
437.1.a. When more than one card is Predicted, the Predicting player looks at that many cards and
Recycles any number of them before putting the rest back on top of their Main Deck in
any order.
437.2. Predicting is a Limited Action.
437.2.a. Players may only Predict cards when instructed to do so by game effects.
437.3. This action, when instructed, is formatted as "Predict X."
437.3.a. If omitted, X is presumed to be 1.
437.4. If a player attempts to Predict more cards than are available in their Main Deck, they will Predict as
many as possible instead.
437.4.a. The Player will not perform a Burn Out as a result of Predicting with too few cards in their
deck.

title: 438. Prevent
text:
438. Prevent
438.1. Preventing damage is the act of reducing the Damage a set of game objects would take.
438.1.a. Prevent is an action that interacts with Damage.
438.1.a.1. Prevent includes any applied Bonus Damage when determining the total damage
being prevented.
438.1.b. Prevent appears in statements that define an amount of damage and the source of the
damage it will affect, as well as the timespan it will be relevant for.
438.1.b.1. Prevent actions are usually formatted as “Prevent the next X [source] damage
that would be dealt to a [unit] this turn.”
438.1.b.1.a. The X is referred to as the Prevent Value.
438.1.b.1.b. X can be “All,” which specifies an infinite amount of damage.
438.1.b.2. Prevent will always apply to the next damage that would be dealt to a unit
affected by the Prevent action.
438.2. When damage is Prevented, it is replaced with an event where the source of the damage deals that
much damage reduced by the Prevent Value tracked on the Unit specifically.
438.2.a. The damage being dealt as a result of Preventing can never be less than 0, but can be 0.
This is equivalent to not dealing damage.
438.3. When damage is dealt this way, reduce the Prevent Value being tracked on the Unit affected by the
Prevent action by the prevented amount.
438.3.a. If the Prevent Value is 0 or less, then Prevent is no longer being tracked on the Unit in
question, and the effect expires.
438.3.b. The reduced value is the newly tracked Prevent Value.
438.3.c. If the Prevent Value is “All” then it remains “All.”
438.4. Damage dealt to a Unit that has that all of that damage Prevented is not considered to have been
dealt to it at all.
438.5. Damage can still be assigned to Units in combat that are affected by Prevent. The damage dealt as
a result of that assignment will be affected by the Prevent action.
438.5.a. Damage can be assigned to a Unit up to a value that would be Lethal considering the
Prevent Value of all Prevent Actions on a Unit, following the normal rules for damage
assignment.
Example: A unit with 2 [M] is being assigned damage in the combat damage step.
The unit has “prevent the first 3 damage I would take each combat.” The unit
would need to be assigned 5 damage in order to have lethal damage assigned to
it.
438.5.b. No amount of damage is ever considered lethal if the Prevent Value is “All.”
438.6. Prevent is a Limited Action.

title: 438. Prevent
text:
438. Prevent (continued)
438.6.a. Players may only Prevent Damage when directed to by Game Effects.
438.7. Prevent is a Delayed Replacement Effect.
See rule 367. Replacement Effects for more information.
See rule 390. Delayed Abilities for more information.

title: 439. Replace
text:
439. Replace
439.1. Replacing is the act of Creating a token in the place of another card or token without playing it
while inheriting all effects or statuses of the game object it replaced.
439.1.a. The replacing token is treated as the same Game Object as the card or token it replaced for
the purposes of Game Effects that target or reference that game object.
Example: A player with Green Father as their legend conquers Navori Fighting Pit.
They choose to place the Green Father conquer effect on the chain after the Navori
Fighting Pit conquer effect. When the Green Father trigger resolves, Navori
Fighting Pit is replaced with Brush. Although the Navori Fighting Pit has been
replaced, the “here” in its triggered ability still can have its information referenced,
because the Brush inherited all statuses and conditions. The unit Navori Fighting
Pit’s triggered ability has targeted will still be a legal target on resolution.
439.2. Replacing is a Limited Action.
439.2.a. The player may Replace cards and tokens when instructed to do so by other game effects.
439.3. This action, when instructed, is formatted as "Replace [X] with [Y]."
439.3.a. The [X] is the target to be Replaced.
439.3.b. The [Y] is the object that will Replace the target.
439.3.b.1. This will always specify a Token to create.
439.4. Replacing is not a subset of Banishing.
439.5. The card or token that is Replaced is placed in Banishment.
439.5.a. While it resides in Banishment, it is considered to have been Replaced and not Banished.
439.6. If a token is Replaced it will stop existing once it begins its occupancy in Banishment.
439.6.a. This does not invalidate the token created, or the act of Replacement.
439.7. Tokens that have been Created through a Replace action can be instructed to be “Swapped back.”
This may also appear as “replace [the token] with the [Game Object] it replaced.”
439.7.a. Swapping Back is an extension of the Replace action.
439.7.b. To Swap Back, the token stops existing and the original card is returned to the space that
the token just occupied, inheriting all current effects and statuses.
439.7.b.1. Any card that has been Replaced by that token or any tokens it Replaced is
eligible to swap back in this way.
439.7.c. If there is nothing in Banishment to swap back to then this object can never swap back.

title: 440. Create
text:
440. Create
440.1. Creating is the act of producing a Game Object that previously did not exist in the game.
440.2. Effects that Create one or more Game Objects will direct where those Game Objects must go - the
Game Objects are Created directly to the zones in question.
440.2.a. Prior to being Created, these Game Objects did not exist outside of the zone they were
Created to. After being Created, they may change zones as appropriate for Game Objects
of their type.
440.2.b. If a zone is not specified by the effect, the Game Object will be created to the appropriate
zone for its type.
440.2.b.1. Permanents will be Created at any location on the Board that they can be played
to.
440.2.b.2. Spells will be Created on the Chain.
440.2.b.3. Runes will be Created at base.
440.2.b.4. Legends will be Created in the Legend Zone.
440.2.b.5. Battlefields will be Created in the Battlefield Zone.
440.2.c. The zone a Game Object is created to can be specified implicitly by the Game Action being
performed.
Example: “Play a 1 [M] Recruit token” specifies a zone where the token is Created to
implicitly, by specifying the token is played and thus created on the chain.
Example: “Create a 1 [M] Recruit token” does not specify a zone, so the Recruit
token will be created at any location on the board that it can be played to.
440.3. An effect that Creates a Game Object will specify the state and nature of the Game Object created.
440.3.a. If the Game Object is a token, it will follow the normal rules for tokens.
See rule 179. Tokens for more information.
440.3.b. If the effect specifies a Game Object is Created for a specific duration, it exists while that
duration is ongoing, and ceases to exist once that duration ends.
440.3.c. If a Non-Token Game Object is Created from a finite set of choices made by a Linked
Ability during deck building, only one of those Game Objects may exist in play at a time. If a
player would Create a Game Object that already exists on the board or on the chain, that
action is Negated.
440.4. Unless specified otherwise by the Game Effect that Creates a Game Object, any such Game Object
is owned by the player who Created it. Control is established as usual for Game Objects of the
appropriate type.
440.4.a. A Created permanent, rune, legend, or spell is controlled by its owner as it is Created.
440.4.b. A Created battlefield is uncontrolled as it is Created.

title: 440. Create
text:
440. Create (continued)
440.5. This action, when instructed, is usually formatted as "Create [X] at [Y]" or “Add [X] to [Y].”
440.6. Creating is a Limited Action.
440.6.a. Players may only Create Game Objects when directed to by Game Effects.

title: 441. Burn
text:
441. Burn
441.1. Burning is the act of moving cards from the top of a player’s Main Deck to their trash.
441.1.a. “When you burn” abilities or other Triggered Abilities that trigger on burning are executed
after burning has occurred.
441.2. This action is formatted as "Burn X."
441.2.a. X is the number of cards to be Burned.
441.3. Burning is a Limited Action.
441.3.a. A player must Burn cards when instructed to do so by game effects or costs.
441.4. When Burning is part of an effect, then a player must Burn as many cards as possible. If instructed to
burn more cards than they have in their main deck, they burn that many cards, burn out and then
burn the rest.
See rule 432. Burn Out for more information.

title: 442. Empower
text:
442. Empower
442.1. Empowering is the act of rendering one or more Game Objects Empowered.
442.1.a. Empowered is a binary state. A Game Object is Empowered or it isn’t.
442.1.b. An Empowered Game Object can not be Empowered.
442.1.c. If a Game Object is instructed to be Empowered when it is already Empowered, nothing
additional happens.
442.1.c.1. Some effects may grant a Game Object permission to be Empowered multiple
times. Such an effect ignores this restriction. For these Game Objects, Empowered
is not a binary state but a stacking status.
442.2. “Empowered” is a state for Game Objects on the board that other game effects and abilities can
reference.
442.2.a. When a Game Object becomes Empowered as a result of the Empower game action, that
is an event that can similarly be referenced by game effects and abilities.
442.3. Empowering is a Limited Action.
442.3.a. Players may only Empower Game Objects when directed to by Game Effects.

title: 443. Disempower
text:
443. Disempower
443.1. Disempowering is the act of removing the Empowered status from one or more Game Objects.
443.1.a. Disempowering affects only cards that are currently Empowered.
443.1.a.1. Game effects that instruct a player to Disempower a card that is not currently
Empowered will do nothing.
443.1.b. Disempowering a Game Object that has multiple Empowered statuses will remove one of
those statuses.
443.2. Disempowering is a Limited Action.
443.2.a. Players may only Disempower Game Objects when directed to by Game Effects.

title: 444. Skip
text:
444. Skip
444.1. Skipping an event is the act of replacing that event with nothing.
444.1.a. Skip is an action that interacts with events and procedures of the turn.
Example: A card reads in part “Choose an enemy unit. Skip the next time that unit
would move this turn.” This is a replacement effect that replaces the event of a unit
moving with nothing.
Example: A card reads in part “Skip your Draw phase.” This is a replacement effect
that replaces a player’s Draw Phase with nothing.
Example: A card reads in part “Choose a player. They skip their next point from
conquering this turn.” This is a replacement effect that replaces the 1 point gained
when conquering with nothing.
444.1.a.1. An event is the singular moment that results from a Game Action being performed
or from a Game Object changing state.
See rule 367. Replacement Effects for more information.
444.1.a.2. Procedures of the turn include turns, phases, steps, and substeps.
444.1.b. Skip actions are usually formatted as “Skip [event or procedure of the turn].”
444.2. When an event or procedure of the turn is Skipped, it is replaced with nothing. Play proceeds
accordingly.
444.2.a. Anything that triggers on the occurrence of the event or procedure of the turn does not
trigger.
444.3. Skip is a Limited Action.
444.3.a. Players may only Skip events or procedures of the turn when directed to by Game Effects.
444.4. Skip is a Replacement Effect.
See rule 367. Replacement Effects for more information.

title: 445. Pay
text:
445. Pay
445.1. Paying a resource is the act of removing that resource from your Rune Pool.
445.1.a. Pay is an action that interacts with Energy and Power.
445.1.b. In order to qualify as a resource to be removed from the Rune Pool, the resource must be [1]
or greater, or [C] or [A] or greater.
Example: [0] is not a resource that can be removed from the Rune Pool. As a cost, it
is paid without performing the pay game action. This cannot be declined.
445.2. When a player is instructed to Pay a resource, that player may remove that resource from their Rune
Pool if it exists there. If they choose not to, the instruction is negated.
445.2.a. If the instruction to Pay resources is part of paying costs for a card or ability, choosing not to
pay those resources will cause the act of playing the card or ability to be undone.
See rule 358. Check Legality for more information.
445.2.b. If the instruction to Pay resources is part of paying any other cost, choosing not to pay those
resources will prevent the execution of the associated effect.
See rule 201. Costs for more information.
445.2.c. Players may activate abilities that Add resources with the Reaction keyword at any time
that they are instructed to Pay resources. Those abilities finalize and resolve immediately,
ignoring normal restrictions.
See rule 430. Add for more information.
445.3. Pay is a Limited Action.
445.3.a. Players may only Pay resources when directed to by Game Effects.

title: 446. Copy
text:
446. Copy
446.1. Copying a Game Object is the act of adding or replacing some or all of the copyable traits of another
Game Object with those of the Copied Game Object.
446.2. Copy Effects are rendered in the Copy Effects layer.
See rule 475. Layers for more information.
446.3. Some Game Objects may be created as a Copy of another Game Object. This is not a Copy Effect.
The Copy in such a case is rendered with the same copyable traits as those of the Game Object it is a
Copy of. It has no printed traits of its own that are subsequently replaced.
Example: Zilean, Time Mage is a unit that reads “Once each turn, if you would play a token
unit while I'm at a battlefield, you may play that token and an additional copy of it instead.”
The additional copy played by Zilean’s replacement effect has no printed traits of its own. Its
printed traits are those of the token it is a copy of.
446.4. Copy is a Limited Action.
446.4.a. Players may only Copy Game Objects when directed to by Game Effects.

title: 448. Moving is a Limited Action.
text:
447. Movement
448. Moving is a Limited Action.
448.1. A Permanent changing its position from any space on the Board to another space on the Board is a
Move, unless it is caused by a corrective Recall or an Attached Permanent changing locations to or
with its Top-Most Card.
See rule 421. Move for more information.
448.2. A card changing game zones does not in itself constitute a Move.
448.3. Moving is instantaneous.
448.3.a. There is no state for Permanents between locations.
448.3.b. Permanents are either at their Origin before Moving or their Destination after Moving.
448.3.c. Moving does not use the Chain, nor is it able to be Reacted to.

title: 449. Moving is defined by the Origin and Destination of the Permanent that is changing locations.
text:
449. Moving is defined by the Origin and Destination of the Permanent that is changing locations.
449.1. The Origin is where the Permanent is starting from.
449.2. The Destination is where the Permanent is going to.
449.2.a. In Modes of Play with more than two players, Battlefields with Staged Combats or
Combats in Progress are Invalid Destinations for Moves of all kinds (Standard Moves or
otherwise) by Units controlled by Players not involved in those Combats or who don't
already have units at that Battlefield.
449.2.b. In Modes of Play with teammates, Battlefields occupied by a player’s teammates are
Invalid Destinations for Moves of all kinds (Standard Moves or otherwise) by Units that
player controls.
449.2.c. If an action would require a Move that would cause a Unit to become present in a Location
where it cannot move for any reason, such as a Battlefield with two players that are not the
controller of the Unit performing this Move action are in a Combat or such a Combat is
Staged, it instead Recalls.
See rule 456. Recalls for more information.
450. Players may choose to move their Units with the Standard Move.
See rule 144. for more information on the Standard Move.

title: 451. Spells, Abilities, or other effects may cause a Move to occur.
text:
451. Spells, Abilities, or other effects may cause a Move to occur.
451.1. The source of the Move will provide details on any restrictions on legality for Destination.
451.2. Units cannot Move to a Battlefield that already has units from 2 other players present by any means.
452. The Destination becomes Contested if it is an Uncontested Battlefield not controlled by the controller of the
Unit or Units that moved.
453. Units may cause a Non-Combat Showdown when they Move.
See rule 341. Showdowns for more information.
454. Units may cause Combat when they Move.
See rule 461. Combat for more information.
455. When a Move action is complete, perform a Cleanup.

title: 457. A Recall is when a Permanent is relocated from anywhere to its Base without it being a Move.
text:
456. Recalls
457. A Recall is when a Permanent is relocated from anywhere to its Base without it being a Move.
458. Recalls are not Moves.
458.1. They do not cause Triggered Abilities to trigger that are triggered by Move actions.
458.2. A Recall causes a Permanent to change locations.
458.3. A Recall cannot be prevented by actions and Game Effects that restrict or block Movement.

title: 459. Gear can be Recalled.
text:
459. Gear can be Recalled.
459.1. When an un-attached non-Unit Gear without deploy is created or played at a battlefield, or is at a
battlefield for any other reason, it is Recalled to its controller's base during the next Cleanup.
Example: An Equipment is attached to a unit at a battlefield, so the Equipment is present at
that battlefield. If the unit dies, the Equipment will be recalled during the next cleanup.
460. Recalls do not affect the state of the Permanent being recalled.
460.1. Unless otherwise stated by the source of the Recall, Damage and statuses of a permanent will all
remain unaffected by a Recall.

title: 462. A Combat occurs when a Cleanup occurs, there are no items on the Chain, there is a staged Combat at a
text:
461. Combat
462. A Combat occurs when a Cleanup occurs, there are no items on the Chain, there is a staged Combat at a
Battlefield, and no Showdown or Combat is ongoing at any other Battlefield.
See rule 318. Cleanups for more information.
462.1. If there is an ongoing Showdown at the Battlefield where the Combat is staged, that Showdown will
become a Combat Showdown and a Combat will be initiated there.

title: 463. Combat is considered Staged if there are units controlled by two opposing players at a Battlefield but the
text:
463. Combat is considered Staged if there are units controlled by two opposing players at a Battlefield but the
Steps of Combat have not been initiated.
463.1. If more than one Battlefield has Units controlled by opposing players at it at the same time, the Turn
Player decides which Combat to resolve first.
463.2. If Staged Combats stop being Staged before the Steps of Combat are initiated, they are not
resolved or executed.
463.3. If a Combat and Showdown are staged at the same Battlefield and the turn player initiates the
Showdown, it will open as a Combat Showdown.

title: 464. Combat can only occur between Units controlled by exactly two players.
text:
464. Combat can only occur between Units controlled by exactly two players.
464.1. In Modes of Play with more than two players, Battlefields with Staged Combats or Combats in
Progress are Invalid Destinations for Moves of all kinds (Standard Moves or otherwise) by Units
controlled by Players not involved in those Combats or who don't already have Units at that
Battlefield.
See rule 449.2.a. for more information on Invalid Destinations.
464.2. In Modes of Play with more than two players, Battlefields with Staged Combats or Combats in
Progress are Invalid to be chosen as a location to play one or more Units by a player not involved in
that Combat by any means.
464.2.a. If an effect would require a Unit be played to a Battlefield with a Staged Combat or a
Combat in Progress, where the controller of the played unit is not a participant, instead the
Unit is played to its controller's Base.
464.2.b. Any subsequent reference to "here" in the corresponding effect is reassigned to the
Controller's Base, where the Unit was played. Any further effects that may be invalidated are
invalidated as if the effect was mistargeted.
See rule 355.6. Targeting for more information on Mistargeting.
464.3. All choices that would result in a Combat occurring between more than two players simultaneously
are invalid and ineligible to be completed.

title: 466. Step 1: The Combat Showdown Step
text:
465. The Steps of Combat
466. Step 1: The Combat Showdown Step
466.1. Combat will open in one of two ways: when a Combat and Showdown are staged at the same
Battlefield and the turn player initiates the Showdown; or when the turn is in a Showdown Open
State and a Combat is staged at the Battlefield where the current Showdown is ongoing.
See rule 318. Cleanups for more information.
466.2. When Combat opens, it either opens with a Combat Showdown, or the current Showdown becomes
a Combat Showdown.
466.2.a. The following Tasks become Outstanding, in the order described:
466.2.b. 1. Start of combat effects happen now. If the Combat opened with a Combat Showdown,
start of showdown effects happen simultaneously.
466.2.c. 2. Establish who is Attacker and who is Defender.
466.2.c.1. The Attacker is the player whose unit(s) applied the Contested status to the
Battlefield.
466.2.c.1.a. If a showdown opens as part of combat, this player gains Focus as the
showdown begins.
466.2.c.1.b. If a showdown was already ongoing when the combat opens, the player
who has Focus maintains their Focus.
466.2.c.2. The Defender is the player who did not apply the Contested status to the
Battlefield.
466.2.c.3. The attacker and defender gain the Attacker or Defender designation now, as
appropriate. Units at the Contested Battlefield controlled by the Attacker or
Defender gain the Attacker or Defender designation now, as appropriate.
466.2.c.3.a. If a Unit controlled by the Attacker or Defender becomes present at this
Battlefield after this moment, it will gain the Attacker or Defender
designation during the Cleanup phase following the action that caused it
to become present, as appropriate for its controller.
466.2.d. 3. Add items to the Combat Chain if establishing Attacker and Defender has caused
Triggered Abilities to become Pending.
466.2.d.1. The Attacking player, who has Focus, places Triggered Abilities on the Chain first,
followed by all non-Defender players in Turn Order, followed by the Defending
Player.
466.2.e. The State Closes if a Combat Chain was created.
466.2.e.1. Otherwise the Combat Showdown continues, with the State Open as normal.
466.2.f. Players proceed with any play on the Chain as normal.

title: 467. Step 2: The Combat Damage Step
text:
467. Step 2: The Combat Damage Step
467.1. If both Attacking and Defending units remain at this battlefield, the following Tasks become
Outstanding, in the specified order:
467.2. 1. When the Showdown closes, Attackers and Defenders resolve Combat Damage at the Battlefield
that was attacked, using their current Might.
467.2.a. Sum the Might of all Attacking Units.
467.2.b. Sum the Might of all Defending Units.
467.2.c. Starting with the Attacker, each player assigns an amount of damage equal to their
summed Might among the other's Units.
467.2.c.1. Assigning Damage is not Dealing Damage.
467.2.c.1.a. When all Damage is assigned, it will be Dealt simultaneously. These
actions are not synonymous.
467.2.c.2. Abilities or effects may influence the order in which damage is assigned.
Reminder: Lethal Damage is non-zero damage equaling or exceeding the
Might of a Unit.
467.2.c.3. Units must have lethal damage assigned to them in full before damage is assigned
to a different Unit.
Example: If a player has 5 damage to distribute among four 3 Might units,
they may not choose to assign 2 damage to one of the units and 1
damage to each of the remaining 3. They must assign 3 damage to one,
and the remaining 2 to another.
467.2.c.4. Units cannot have more damage assigned to them than the minimum required to
constitute lethal damage unless no further units remain to have damage assigned
to them.
Example: If a player has 5 damage to distribute among four 3 Might units
and those units each have 1 damage already marked on them, that player
may not assign more than 2 damage to any of those units.
467.2.c.4.a. If the damage assigned to a Unit is modified to or replaced by an amount
of damage larger than the initial value, the assigning player must choose
the minimum applied value such that the unit would take lethal damage.
Example: A unit with 3 [M] is being assigned damage in the
combat damage step. There are other units without damage
assigned to them with the same controller. The unit has a
delayed replacement effect applied to it that reads “Double all
damage that would be dealt to it this turn.” When assigning
damage, the assigning player can only choose to assign 1 or 2
damage to this unit—when doing so, the assigned damage is
doubled to 2 or 4 damage respectively. The minimum applied
value such that the unit would take lethal damage in this way is
4 damage.
467.2.c.5. When assigning damage in this way, passive abilities and replacement effects that
would apply to the resulting damage are considered to apply to the assignment
instead.
Example: A unit with 2 [M] is being assigned damage in the combat
damage step. The unit has “prevent the first 3 damage I would take each
combat.” The unit would need to be assigned 5 damage in order to have
lethal damage assigned to it.
Example: The attacking player is assigning their 3 [M] worth of damage to
two defending units with 2 [M] each. One of the units has a delayed
replacement effect applied to it that reads “Double all damage that would
be dealt to it this turn.” The attacking player assigns two damage to the
other defending unit, then when assigning damage to the unit with the
delayed replacement effect they assign 2 damage to it; 1 damage that
doubles to 2 damage as it is assigned to the unit. When that damage is
dealt, it doesn’t get doubled again—the doubling is considered to have
already happened during damage assignment.
Example: The attacking player is assigning their 3 [M] worth of damage to
a 2 [M] unit. That unit has a prevent value of two being applied to it, as well
as the effect of Lotus Trap, doubling the damage dealt to them. Both of
these replacement effects apply to the assignment of damage, in the
order of the controller of the 2 [M] unit’s choice. If they choose to order the
replacement effects so that the prevent value is applied first, the unit will
prevent 2 of the assigned damage, then the last 1 point of damage will be
doubled to 2. The unit will have 4 damage assigned to it. When damage is
dealt, the unit will take 2 damage. If they choose the other order, the unit
will have 6 damage assigned to it, 2 of which will be prevented. When
damage is dealt, the unit will take 4 damage.

title: 467. Step 2: The Combat Damage Step
text:
467. Step 2: The Combat Damage Step (continued)
467.2.c.6. A player must obey all requirements and restrictions on damage assignment if
able.
Example: A player is assigning damage to the following units: a unit with
Tank ("I must be assigned combat damage first."); a unit with Backline ("I
must be assigned combat damage last."); and another unit without any
abilities. That player must assign combat damage first to the unit with
Tank, then to the unit with no abilities, then to the unit with Backline.
467.2.c.7. If multiple Units have abilities or effects that require a player to assign them
damage with the same priority, that player may assign damage to those units in
any order.
Example: A player is assigning damage to the following units: two units
with Tank ("I must be assigned combat damage first.") and one unit with
no abilities. That player chooses one of the units with Tank and assigns
combat damage to it. Then they must assign any remaining damage first
to the other unit with Tank, then to the unit with no abilities.
467.2.c.8. If a Unit has one or more Abilities or effects applying to it that demand it be
assigned damage in a specific way that is exclusionary, then the assigning player
chooses only one of those abilities to apply when assigning damage.
Example: Caitlyn, Patrolling with the Backline ability ("I must be assigned
combat damage last.") has been given the Tank ability ("I must be
assigned combat damage first."). A player is assigning damage to this
Caitlyn with Tank and two units with no abilities. That player can’t fulfill
both of Caitlyn’s damage requirements, so they may choose to assign
damage to Caitlyn first, fulfilling the Tank requirement, or last, fulfilling the
Backline requirement. They can’t choose to apply damage to Caitlyn in
between the other two units, because that wouldn’t fulfill either
requirement.
467.2.c.9. If there is more than one unit in which this situation applies to, each unit is dealt
with individually. The assigning player chooses which ability or effect applies, and
then resolves the assignment. If this creates a situation where now more than one
unit must be assigned with the same priority, those units may be assigned
damage in any order as normal within that priority.
Example: Two copies of Caitlyn, Patrolling with the Backline ability ("I
must be assigned combat damage last.") have been given the Tank ability
("I must be assigned combat damage first."). A player assigning damage
to these two Caitlyns and one unit with no abilities could choose to fulfill
both Caitlyns’ Tank requirements by assigning them both damage before
the other unit.
467.2.c.10. If a unit cannot be dealt damage, then no amount of damage can be considered
lethal. Such a unit is exempt from any considerations of mandatory assignment.
Example: Kayn, Unleashed says “If I have moved twice this turn, I don't
take damage.” While Kayn can’t take damage, it is ignored for the
purposes of assigning lethal damage in combat.
Example: Counter Strike says “Choose a unit. The next time that unit
would be dealt damage this turn, prevent it.” The unit in question has a
replacement effect applied to it, but it still can be dealt damage. Thus, it is
not exempt from considerations of mandatory assignment.

title: 467. Step 2: The Combat Damage Step
text:
467. Step 2: The Combat Damage Step (continued)
467.2.d. Deal Damage to each unit equal to the amount assigned to it.
467.3. 2. Skip the FEPR process and cancel any outstanding tasks. Proceed to the Resolution Step.

title: 468. Step 3: The Resolution Step
text:
468. Step 3: The Resolution Step
468.1. 1. Perform a Combat Cleanup.
468.1.a. Invoke a Combat Special Cleanup.
468.1.a.1. Insert “3c. Heal all Units.”
468.1.a.2. Insert “3d. Recall Attackers present at the Battlefield if Defenders are still
present.”
See rule 456. Recalls for more information.
468.2. The following Task becomes Outstanding:
Reminder: Resolve any items on the chain from dealing combat damage and the Combat
Cleanup and associated FEPR before performing this step.
468.3. 1. Determine Combat Result
468.3.a. A Player has won a combat if they received either the attacker or defender designation and
are the only Player that has units remaining at this battlefield during this step.
468.3.b. A Player has lost a combat if they received either the attacker or defender designation and
are the only Player that does not have any units remaining at this battlefield during this
step.
468.3.c. Units at this battlefield inherit the same combat result as their controllers.
468.3.d. There is “No Result” if units were recalled during step 3d of the Combat Cleanup, if both
Players have units present during this task, or if neither player has units present during
this task.
468.3.d.1. If “No Result” was reached, and both players have units remaining, stage a
Showdown and a Combat at this battlefield.
468.4. The following Task becomes Outstanding:
Reminder: Resolve any items on the chain from determining combat result and associated
FEPR before performing this step.
468.5. 1. If no Showdown or Combat is staged at this location, the player with Units remaining here
Establishes Control if they didn’t already control this Battlefield.
468.5.a. Clear the Contested Status.
468.5.b. If there are no Units remaining here controlled by any player, the Battlefield becomes
Uncontrolled.
468.5.c. Remove all Hidden cards from this Battlefield that do not share a controller with the
Battlefield.
468.5.d. Establishing Control results in a Conquer if that player has not yet scored this Battlefield
this turn.
See rule 188. Control for more information on Control.
See rule 471.1. for more information on Conquering.
468.5.e. This does not have to be the player that applied Contested to the Battlefield.
468.6. The following Task becomes Outstanding:
Reminder: Resolve any items on the chain from establishing control and associated FEPR
before performing this step.
468.7. 1. Combat ends.

title: 468. Step 3: The Resolution Step
text:
468. Step 3: The Resolution Step (continued)
468.7.a. Remove Attacker and Defender Designation from all Units and Players.
468.7.b. At the end of Combat or Combat ends effects take place.
468.7.c. All “this combat” effects expire simultaneously.

title: 470. Scoring is the act of a Player seizing or maintaining control over Battlefields they have not yet Scored this
text:
469. Scoring
470. Scoring is the act of a Player seizing or maintaining control over Battlefields they have not yet Scored this
turn.
470.1. Scoring is a distinct process from Gaining Points. Scoring may result in a player Gaining Points, but
the two are not intrinsically linked.
470.2. Card text will refer to the process of Gaining Points in the following way: “Score X points.” The “score”
in this text does not refer to the process of Scoring.
470.3. Card text will refer to the process of Scoring using the word “score” without referring to some
number of points. This does refer to the process of Scoring.

title: 471. A player Scores in one of two ways:
text:
471. A player Scores in one of two ways:
471.1. Conquer: A player gains Control of a Battlefield they did not yet Score this turn.
471.1.a. In Modes of Play with teammates, Battlefields under the Control of a teammate during
the scoring step of the Beginning Phase of a player’s turn are also disqualified from being
Scored through Conquer by any means by that player’s team.
471.1.b. A player will gain control of a Battlefield after establishing Control.
471.2. Hold: A player maintains Control of a Battlefield they did not yet Score this turn during their
Beginning Phase.
472. A player may only Score, from either method, once per Battlefield per turn.

title: 473. When a player Scores, two things occur:
text:
473. When a player Scores, two things occur:
473.1. The player Gains up to one Point, depending on their current score.
473.1.a. The Final Point has additional restrictions.
473.1.a.1. Notably, points Gained from sources that are not Conquer are not beholden to
these restrictions.
473.1.b. When a player tries to Gain a Point through a Conquer, and their current Point Total is 1
point from the Victory Score of the Mode of Play or higher, the following occurs:
473.1.b.1. If the player has Scored every Battlefield this turn, that player Gains the Final
Point. If the player has not Scored every Battlefield this turn, that player draws a
card instead.
473.2. Trigger Score abilities at the Battlefield that Scored.
473.2.a. Conquer abilities trigger at a Battlefield that was Conquered.
473.2.b. Hold abilities trigger at a Battlefield that was Held.
473.2.c. These will only trigger when the Battlefield is Scored; I.E. These cannot be triggered more
than once per turn for a player.
474. When a cleanup occurs and a player has accrued Points greater than or equal to the Victory Score for their
Mode of Play, and if they have more points than every opponent, they Win the Game.

title: 476. Layers are the mechanism in which Game Effects alter the Traits, Intrinsic Abilities, or other properties of
text:
475. Layers
476. Layers are the mechanism in which Game Effects alter the Traits, Intrinsic Abilities, or other properties of
Game Objects.
477. Layers are an organizational structure.
477.1. Layers only serve to structure the application and order that Game Effects apply to Game Objects to
maintain consistency.

title: 478. The layers are applied repeatedly until all effects operating on an object have been applied once and no
text:
478. The layers are applied repeatedly until all effects operating on an object have been applied once and no
changes have been processed.
478.1. Layers are applied and evaluated continuously. All Game Objects have their layers updated in the
same instant, but each Game Object is treated separately and individually when evaluating layers.
478.1.a. If evaluating a Game Effect’s applicability depends on information from one or more other
Game Objects, that Game Effect has an object level Dependency. Pause evaluating the
layers of the dependent Game Object and evaluate the layer effects of those Game Objects
whose information is referenced. Continue once the applicability of that Game Effect has
been established or disqualified.
Example: A 4 [M] unit reads in part “While I’m [Mighty], I’m a Yeti.” Another unit
reads in part “I have all tags of units you control.” When the 4 [M] unit is buffed, the
layers for all game objects are evaluated. While evaluating the layers for the second
unit, it requires us to pause and evaluate the layers for all other units. When we’re
evaluating the layers for the 4 [M] unit, after all is said and done, the unit has the
Yeti tag. Once we’ve evaluated all units, we go back to evaluating the second unit,
and at that time it has the Yeti tag as well.
478.1.b. If a Game Object has an object level dependency with a Game Object that itself has an
object level dependency with a third Game Object and so on, determine the final point of
the dependency chain and evaluate the layer effects of that Game Object first, continuing
up the dependency chain until all Game Objects have had their layer effects evaluated.

title: 478. The layers are applied repeatedly until all effects operating on an object have been applied once and no
text:
478. The layers are applied repeatedly until all effects operating on an object have been applied once and no (continued)
478.1.c. If a dependency chain loops back around on itself, identify the minimum set of Game
Objects in the loop and evaluate their layer effects simultaneously, layer by layer. If any of
them have Game Effects that reference Game Objects from outside the set, pause and
evaluate those Game Objects first before continuing with the set.
Example: A 4 [M] unit reads “If there is a [Mighty] enemy unit here, I have +5 [M].”
Both players control one of these units at a battlefield during combat. Each one is
buffed. A third player plays Siphon Power, which reads “Choose a battlefield. Give
friendly units there +1 [M] this turn, and enemy units there -1 [M] this turn, to a
minimum of 1 [M].” Both of the units there are given -1 [M]. Because they have
effects that reference each other, they have a dependency chain. After evaluating
their layers simultaneously, layer by layer, both units will be 4 [M].
478.2. Layers are applied in sequence. Each effect in them is applied as soon as able, and only a single time
across all sequences.
478.3. When a sequence of applications completes, recur the process, and evaluate each layer again
applying any effects that may now be applicable.
478.4. The removal or disqualification of an effect is separate from the application of the effect, but still can
only be applied once.
Example: Fiora, Victorious has printed Might 4 and says “While I'm Mighty, I have Deflect,
Ganking, and Shield.” If a player places a buff on Fiora, her Might is increased in the
Arithmetic layer, after the layer for Ability-Altering Effects. The Ability-Altering Effect layer is
then re-checked and the abilities Deflect, Ganking, and Shield applied. Since each effect has
been applied once and there are no other effects to apply, Fiora’s characteristics are
finalized as 5 Might with Deflect, Ganking, and Shield. While a buffed Fiora, Victorious is in
combat as a defender, an additional +1 Might will be applied in the Arithmetic layer, giving
her 6 Might and the 3 keywords.
Example: A buffed Fiora, Victorious is in combat as a defender when her buff is removed.
Reevaluating the layers in sequence, she no longer gains Deflect, Ganking, and Shield
during the Ability-Altering Effect layer, so when the Arithmetic layer is evaluated, neither the
buff (which is gone) nor Shield (which she no longer has) apply. She goes directly from 6
Might with three keywords to 4 Might with no keywords.

title: 479. Layers are applied in the following order:
text:
479. Layers are applied in the following order:
479.1. 1. Copy Effects
479.1.a. This layer deals with all copy effects.
479.1.b. When a Copy effect is applied to a Game Object, the traits specified by the Copy Effect
replace or are added to the Copyable Traits of the Game Object being Copied as specified
by the effect. If no traits are specified by a Copy Effect, all traits of the Game Object are
replaced with those of the Copied Game Object.
Example: A player triggers Leblanc, Deceiver’s hold effect and plays a Reflection
token, making it a copy of Honest Broker. That player then plays Mirror Image,
targeting the Reflection token. When the Mirror Image Reflection token is played,
it copies all of the copyable traits of the original Reflection token - which are
currently those of Honest Broker which it is a copy of. That player will have three
units named Honest Broker in play, two of which are token Copies with Temporary.
479.1.b.1. The copyable traits of a Game Object are all of the printed—or if a copy effect is
applied, copied—traits of that Game Object. In the case of a Token, they are the
traits the token had when it was Created.
Example: The copyable traits include the printed versions of the following
traits: Name, Supertype, Type, Tags, Cost, Domain, Rules Text, Effect Text,
Might, Might Bonus, Flavor Text, Art
479.1.c. Copyable traits of a Game Object are distinct from the actual traits of that Game Object,
which may be modified by subsequent applied Layer effects.
479.1.d. Effects for this layer can be identified by the phrase "copy" in the text.
Example: Svellsongur is an Equipment that reads in part “As this is attached to a
unit, copy that unit's text to this Equipment's effect text for as long as this is
attached to it.” This is a copy effect that is applied in this layer.
479.2. 2. Trait-Altering Effects
479.2.a. This layer deals with effects that grant, remove, or replace inherent traits of Game Objects.
Name
Supertype
Type
Tags
Controller
Cost
Domain
Base Might
Base Might Bonus
479.2.b. Effects for this layer can be identified by the phrase "become(s)", "give," "is," or "are" in the
text.
Example: A permanent has the ability "Other friendly units are Yordles." Other
friendly units gain the Yordle tag in this layer.
479.3. 3. Ability-Altering Effects

title: 479. Layers are applied in the following order:
text:
479. Layers are applied in the following order: (continued)
479.3.a. This layer deals with non-Copy effects that grant, remove, or replace the abilities or rules text
of Game Objects.
Keywords
Passive Abilities
Appending rules text
Removing rules text
Effect Text
479.3.b. Effects for this layer can be identified by the phrase "become(s)," "give," "lose(s)," "have,"
"has," "is," or "are" in the text.
Example: A permanent has the ability "Other friendly units have [Vision]." Other
friendly units gain the Vision keyword in this layer.
479.3.c. Abilities of Effect Text of Attached cards are appended in this layer.
479.4. 4. Arithmetic Effects
479.4.a. This layer deals with the mathematics of increasing and decreasing the numeric values of
the traits of Game Objects.
Might
Energy Cost
Power Cost
479.4.b. When an arithmetic effect from a source that is not a passive ability has a limitation that
applies, it is limited at the time of its application, and is “remembered” at that limited level
for the duration of its effect. This process is called “snapshotting.”
Example: If an effect gives a unit “-4 [M] to a min of 1 this turn” choosing a unit with
2 [M], then the effect will generate -1 [M] this turn.
Example: A unit reads “Units you control here have their Might increased to 5 [M].”
This is a passive ability, so it will not snapshot.
Example: A spell reads “Increase a friendly unit’s Might to 5 [M].” This effect is
applied once, with an unlimited duration. Because it isn’t from a passive ability, it
will snapshot.
479.4.c. Players cannot increase a numeric attribute by a negative amount. If an effect would
instruct a player to do so, they increase it by 0 instead.
Example: A player plays Last Stand, which reads “Double a friendly unit's Might this
turn. Give it Temporary.” The player declares a 2 [M] unit as the target during
finalization. In reaction to Last Stand, an opponent plays Eclipse targeting the 2 [M]
unit. When Last Stand resolves, the unit is -2 [M]. Last Stand instructs its controller
to increase the unit’s Might by its current amount, -2, when the double action is
performed. This is not possible, so the unit’s Might is increased by 0 instead.
479.4.d. Might Bonuses of Attached cards are applied in this layer.
479.4.e. This layer applies arithmetic in the following way.
479.4.e.1. 1. Increases
479.4.e.1.a. Positive values, or increases, to Might are applied first.
479.4.e.1.b. If there is a restriction or limitation to this increase and it isn’t from a
passive ability, the limitation is “snapshotted” for the duration of the effect.
479.4.e.2. 2. Decreases
479.4.e.2.a. Negative values, or decreases, to Might are applied last.
479.4.e.2.b. If there is a restriction or limitation to this decrease and it isn’t from a
passive ability, the limitation is “snapshotted” for the duration of the effect.

title: 479. Layers are applied in the following order:
text:
479. Layers are applied in the following order: (continued)
479.4.f. Effects for this layer can be identified by the phrase "give,” “swap,” "increase," "decrease,"
"cost ... less," "cost ... more," "-X,” or “+X,” in the text.
Example: An effect says “I cost [1] less for each card you've played this turn, to a
minimum of [1].” The cost is modified in this layer.

title: 480. If more than one effect applies to the same Game Object in the Same Layer, or to each other in the same
text:
480. If more than one effect applies to the same Game Object in the Same Layer, or to each other in the same
layer, then both effects will apply but their order may be determined by Dependency.
480.1. A Dependency is established if:
480.1.a. Applying one of the effects alters the existence of the other; or
480.1.b. Applying one of the effects alters the number of objects the other effect can influence; or
480.1.c. Applying one of the effects alters the outcome when applying the other.

title: 481. To determine which effect Depends on another, determine which of the prior criteria applies, and then also
text:
481. To determine which effect Depends on another, determine which of the prior criteria applies, and then also
which effect’s evaluation is altered by the sequence of applications. That effect is said to Depend on the other.
Example: A unit with 4 [M] is under the effects of a passive ability that reads “Units you control here
have their Might increased to 5 [M].” Its controller plays Discipline on the unit, giving it +2 [M]. When
applying Layer alterations, both effects are applied in the same layer. If we apply the passive ability
first, the passive ability will give +1 [M] while the Discipline effect will give +2 [M]. If we apply them in
the other order, the Discipline effect will give +2 [M], and the passive ability will give +0 [M]. The
passive ability is altered by the sequence of applications, so it depends on the Discipline effect.
481.1. If both effects are altered by the application of the other, no Dependency can be established.
Example: A unit with 4 [M] is under the effects of a passive ability that reads “Units you
control here have their Might increased to 5 [M].” Its controller plays a spell that reads “Give a
unit +2 [M], to a maximum of 5 [M].” If we apply the passive ability first, the passive ability will
apply +1 [M] and the spell effect will apply +0 [M]. If we apply the spell effect first, it will apply
+1 [M] while the passive ability applies +0 [M]. Both effects are altered by the sequence of
applications, so we can’t establish a dependency.
481.2. To resolve a dependency, the effects within the same layer that created the dependency must be
applied such that:
1. Identify which effect Depends on the other within the Layer.
2. Apply the effect that is depended on first.
3. Immediately apply the effect that Depends on the first effect next.
Example: A unit with 4[M] is under the effects of a passive ability that reads “Units you
control here have their Might increased to 5 [M].” Its controller plays Discipline on the unit.
As previously established, the passive ability depends on the Discipline effect. We apply the
Discipline effect first, giving the unit +2 [M], and then immediately apply the passive ability
that depends on it. The unit’s final Might is 6 [M].

title: 482. If more than one effect applies to the same Game Object in the same layer but no dependency is established,
text:
482. If more than one effect applies to the same Game Object in the same layer but no dependency is established,
then Timestamp order is applied to the effects within that layer and sublayer
482.1. When an effect begins applying, it establishes a time for which it is compared against other Game
Effects for purposes of resolving Layered effects as its Timestamp.
482.1.a. Timestamps are not rote values.
482.1.b. Timestamps are relative comparisons between effects and when they began applying to
the game.
482.1.c. Timestamps are not referenced by Game Effects in any way. They are only used to finalize
layered effects.
482.2. When Rules Text becomes Inactive for any reason, it loses its Timestamp. When it ceases to be
Inactive, a new Timestamp is established.
482.3. Effects are applied such that the earliest Timestamp within each Layer and Sublayer applies first,
followed by other Effects in that Layer and Sublayer in chronological order.

title: 484. There are multiple methods of playing Riftbound.
text:
483. Modes of Play
484. There are multiple methods of playing Riftbound.

title: 485. A Mode of Play must define several variables for the game.
text:
485. A Mode of Play must define several variables for the game.
485.1. Number of Players: How many people are playing the game.
485.2. Formation of Players: How the players are organized while playing.
485.2.a. This defines if a player is alone or on a team.
485.2.b. This defines the number of opponents.
485.3. Victory Score: The point total a player or team must reach to win.
485.3.a. Victory Scores can be any positive number.
485.4. Battlefield Count: Determines how many Battlefields are in play, contributed by players, during
play.
485.4.a. This may influence deck building requirements in competitive settings.
485.4.b. This may involve utilizing less Battlefields than there are players.
485.5. Setup: Any changes to initial setup required for this mode.
485.6. Format: Conditions to win or additional rules added over play.
485.7. First Turn Process: Adjustments to each player's first turn.
485.8. Unique Rules
485.8.a. If any, they will be appended here.

title: 487. 1v1 (Duel)
text:
486. Sanctioned Modes
487. 1v1 (Duel)
487.1. 2 Players
487.2. 1v1
1 opponent each
No teams
487.3. Victory Score: 8
487.4. Battlefield Count: 2
487.4.a. Each player provides three (3) Battlefields, included in their deck during deck building. Only
1 will be used, chosen during setup.
487.5. Setup: Each player randomly selects one (1) of their three (3) Battlefields. The other two are removed
and will not be used for this game. The selected Battlefields are placed simultaneously in the
Battlefield Zone.
487.6. Format: Best of 1. The first player to reach the Victory Score in Points wins the Match.
487.7. First Turn Process: The player going second channels an extra Rune from their Rune Deck during
their first Channel Phase of the game.

title: 488. 1v1 (Match)
text:
488. 1v1 (Match)
488.1. 2 Players
488.2. 1v1
1 opponent each
No teams
488.3. Victory Score: 8
488.4. Battlefield Count: 2
488.4.a. Each player provides three (3) Battlefields, included in their deck during deck building. Only
1 will be used, chosen during setup.
488.5. Setup: Each player selects one (1) of their three (3) Battlefields. The other two are set aside and will
not be used for this round of play. The selected Battlefields are placed simultaneously in the
Battlefield Zone. After this game, if a player won, the Battlefields that were used are to be removed
and not selected again for this Match. One of the remaining Battlefields that were set aside must be
chosen instead.
488.5.a. If no player won a game, the battlefields presented for that game may be reused in a
subsequent game.
488.6. Format: Best of 3. The first player to reach the Victory Score in Points wins the game. The winner of
that game earns One Game Win. Players then reset the game state, remove the Battlefields in play
from the game, choose new Battlefields from those set aside, and play again. The first player to earn
Two Game Wins wins the match.
488.6.a. This format may be played as best of 5. In such a case, during games 4 and 5 of the match
players may present a battlefield that has been removed from the game.
488.6.a.1. Players may only re-use a battlefield in this way if they have already presented each
of their battlefields at least once during the match.
488.6.a.2. Players may not present a battlefield more than twice in a match when re-using
battlefields in this way.
488.7. First Turn Process: The player going second channels an extra Rune from their Rune Deck during
their first Channel Phase of the game.

title: 489. FFA3 (Skirmish)
text:
489. FFA3 (Skirmish)
489.1. 3 Players
489.2. FFA
2 opponents each
No teams
489.3. Victory Score: 8
489.4. Battlefield Count: 3
489.4.a. Each player provides three (3) Battlefields, included in their deck during deck building. Only
1 will be used, chosen during setup.
489.5. Setup: Each player randomly selects one (1) of their three (3) Battlefields. The other two are
discarded and will not be used for this game. The selected Battlefields are placed simultaneously
between the three Players before play and will be used for this game.
489.6. Format: Best of 1. The first player to reach the Victory Score in Points wins the Match.
489.7. First Turn Process: The player going first does not draw a card during their first Draw Phase of the
game. The player going last channels an extra Rune from their Rune Deck during their first Channel
Phase of the game.

title: 490. FFA4 (War)
text:
490. FFA4 (War)
490.1. 4 Players
490.2. FFA
3 opponents each
No teams
490.3. Victory Score: 8
490.4. Battlefield Count: 3
490.4.a. Each player provides three (3) Battlefields, included in their deck during deck building.
490.4.b. The player who is taking the first turn removes their Battlefields. They will not be used.
490.5. Setup: Each player who is not going first randomly selects one (1) of their three (3) Battlefields. The
other two are removed and will not be used for this game. The selected Battlefields are placed
simultaneously between the players before play and will be used for this game.
490.6. Format: Best of 1. The first player to reach the Victory Score in Points wins the Match.
490.7. First Turn Process: The player going first does not draw a card during their first Draw Phase of the
game. The player going last channels an extra Rune from their Rune Deck during their first Channel
Phase of the game.

title: 491. 2v2 (Magma Chamber)
text:
491. 2v2 (Magma Chamber)
491.1. 4 Players
491.2. 2v2
2 opponents each
1 teammate
491.3. Victory Score: 11
491.4. Battlefield Count: 3
491.4.a. Each player provides three (3) Battlefields, included in their deck during deck building.
491.5. Setup:
491.5.a. Each player who is not going first randomly selects one (1) of their three (3) Battlefields. The
other two are removed and will not be used for this game. The selected Battlefields are
placed simultaneously between the players before play and will be used for this game.
491.5.b. The player who is taking the first turn removes their Battlefields. They will not be used.
491.5.c. Turn order alternates teams.
491.5.c.1. The first player will be followed by an opponent, then the first player's teammate,
then the first opponent's teammate, and so on.
491.5.c.2. If allies are sitting across from each other, turn order proceeds clockwise as normal.
491.5.c.3. If allies are sitting next to each other, turn order is passed across the table.
491.6. Format: Best of 1. The first team to reach the Victory Score in Points wins the Match.
491.6.a. Teammates win or lose together.
491.6.a.1. If one player Concedes, then the entire team loses.
491.6.a.2. If one player Loses, then the entire team loses.
491.6.a.3. If one player Wins, then the entire team wins.
491.7. First Turn Process: The player going first does not draw a card during their first Draw Phase of the
game. The player going last channels an extra Rune from their Rune Deck during their first Channel
Phase of the game.
491.8. Unique Rules
491.8.a. Players may play spells or activate abilities during their Teammate's Turn. In order to do so,
their Teammate will invite them to play a spell or activate an ability using their own Priority.
491.8.b. A Battlefield can only be Scored, via Conquering or Holding, once per team per turn.
491.8.b.1. Battlefields controlled during the Scoring Step in the Beginning Phase of a
player's turn by that player's teammate are disqualified from being scored by that
Team, that turn.
Example: A player may not induce their partner to retreat, and then
conquer a Battlefield their teammate was controlling.
491.8.c. Control is not shared.
491.8.c.1. Players may not Hide cards at Battlefields controlled by their Teammate.
491.8.c.2. Players may not issue Standard Movement to their Teammate's Units.
491.8.d. Points are shared by a team.
491.8.d.1. Both players on a team have the same number of Victory Points.
491.8.d.2. If a player gains or loses points, their team gains or loses those points.
491.8.d.3. If a spell or ability references or checks a player gaining or losing points, that ability
checks whether that player’s team gains or loses points.

title: 491. 2v2 (Magma Chamber)
text:
491. 2v2 (Magma Chamber) (continued)
491.8.e. Friendly describes controlled Game Objects by a player or their Teammate.
Example: "When you play me, ready a friendly unit" could target a player's own
Units or their teammate's Units.
491.8.f. Hands are Private Information. Players may show their Private Information to one or more
players at any time during play, including their teammate.
491.8.f.1. Revealing Cards is still a game action and cannot be done unless instructed.
See rule 425. Reveal for more information.
491.8.g. The Final Point has an adjustment to the criteria when scoring.
491.8.g.1. When scoring the Final Point from Conquer during their or a teammate’s turn, a
player must Score each Battlefield in the same turn, excepting any that were
occupied by their ally during the scoring step of that turn’s Beginning Phase.
See rule 469. Scoring for more information.
491.8.g.2. No other changes to Final Point restrictions.
491.8.h. Teammates may not utilize the same Champion Legend.
491.8.i. Teammates may not utilize the same Battlefields.

title: 650. A player may concede at any time.
text:
649. Conceding
650. A player may concede at any time.

title: 651. When a player concedes, they are removed from the game in progress.
text:
651. When a player concedes, they are removed from the game in progress.
651.1. If only one other player is remaining after a player has conceded, the player remaining Wins.
651.2. If more than one player remains after a concession, follow the steps for the Removal of a Player.
651.3. Removal of a player involves them no longer being able to make choices or otherwise influence the
game.
651.4. If the player has Teammates due to the Mode of Play, that player’s Teammates also lose and are
removed from the game.

title: 652. If the game continues, follow these steps for Removal of a Player.
text:
652. If the game continues, follow these steps for Removal of a Player.
652.1. Banish all permanents, runes, and facedown cards they currently control and all permanents, runes,
and facedown cards they own.
652.2. Remove the Battlefield they contributed to the game if it is in use.
652.2.a. If it was in use, Replace it with a token battlefield with no abilities.
652.2.b. Any units or hidden cards there do not move and are otherwise unaffected by this process.
See rule 439. Replace for more information.
652.2.c. If the removed battlefield was applying any continuous effects, those continuous effects
immediately cease, which may cause changes in the characteristics of units or hidden cards
there.
Example: A battlefield reads "Units here have +1 [M]." If that battlefield's owner
concedes and the battlefield is removed from the game as a result, units there
immediately cease to get +1 [M].
652.3. Remove all cards they own from the game.
652.4. Counter all spells and abilities of all types controlled by the player that has conceded.
652.5. Proceed with the game.
652.5.a. Turn
652.5.a.1. If the removed player was the Turn Player, play proceeds in Turn Order to the next
available player in order.
652.5.b. Focus
652.5.b.1. If the removed player had Focus in a Showdown, the next Player in order receives
Focus.
652.5.b.2. If the player being removed creates a state where all Players have Passed their
Focus, the Showdown ends and play proceeds as necessary, E.G. Combat is
resolved or a Cleanup is completed.
652.5.c. Priority
652.5.c.1. If the removed player had Priority during a Chain, the next Player in order receives
Priority.
652.5.c.2. If the player being removed creates a state where all Players have passed Priority,
then the most recent spell or ability on the Chain will resolve with Priority being
re-established as appropriate for the state after the resolution of that spell or
ability.

title: 702. Buffs are counters placed on Units.
text:
700. Additional Rules
701. Buffs
702. Buffs are counters placed on Units.
702.1. Buffs can be tracked with a buff reminder card from a Riftbound booster pack or with any spare
object in your surroundings.
702.2. Buffs can be added or spent.
702.2.a. To Buff a Unit, a player chooses a Unit and then places a buff on it. That Unit is Buffed for as
long as the buff remains on it.
702.2.b. Spending a Buff removes a single Buff counter from a Unit.
702.2.b.1. A buff cannot be spent from a Unit that does not have a buff.
702.2.b.2. A player can only spend buffs on units they control.
702.3. There can only be one Buff on a Unit at a time.
702.3.a. If a Buff is added, or instructed to be added, on a Unit that already has a Buff, it is not
placed instead.
703. Each Buff individually contributes +1 Might to a Unit.
704. Buffs are Game Objects and may be referenced, counted, or affected by other effects as specified.
704.1. Buffs are counters, and thus are not targeted by spells and abilities.
See rule 741. Counters for more information.
705. If a Unit leaves play, remove all Buffs from it.
705.1. Champions do not retain Buffs in the Champion Zone, even if they return there somehow.

title: 707. Mighty is a description that applies to some units. Other game effects can check whether a unit is Mighty.
text:
706. Mighty
707. Mighty is a description that applies to some units. Other game effects can check whether a unit is Mighty.
708. A Unit "is Mighty" as long as its Might is 5 or greater.
709. A Unit "becomes Mighty" at the moment its Might changes from being less than 5 to being 5 or greater.
Example: A Unit with Might 4 that gets +1 [M] becomes Mighty.
Example: A Unit with Might 5 that gets +1 [M] does not become Mighty, because it was already
Mighty.

title: 710. Units on the board are evaluated according to their current Might.
text:
710. Units on the board are evaluated according to their current Might.
Example: A unit with a base Might of 3 is targeted by a spell that reads "A unit gets +3 [M] this turn."
